newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH OKD MINING SEES LOWER NET IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: CZECH OKD MINING SEES LOWER NET IN 1997.

text.p: The largest Czech coal mining concern, OKD a.s. expects a drop in 1997 net profit to 50 million crowns after a forecast rise in pre-tax earnings of about four million crowns to 76 million crowns this year.
"Because of a protracted mining recession at home and abroad... (net) profit should be next year up to 50 million crowns," general director Ivan Dzida told a news conference.
OKD remains one of the largest Czech companies with end-1995 assets totalling 44 billion crowns, but its profit to assets ratio is one of the worst.

The company reported preliminary nine-month gross profit on Tuesday of 46 million crowns with operating profit of 93.9 million, but comparative results for the January-September period were not available.
The state still holds a 43 percent stake in OKD, and officials with the state-run National Property Fund (FNM) have said that it is one of the "least prepared" companies for further privatisation.
